title: Growth of quartet correlations in neutron-rich Tellurium isotopes within quartet Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer theory
authors: Yixin Guo, Hiroyuki Sagawa, Masaaki Kimura
abstract: Quartet correlations in neutron-rich Te isotopes are investigated within the quartet Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) framework. Taking \(^{100}\)Sn as an inert core, we consider two valence protons and valence neutrons occupying the \(2d_{5/2}\oplus1g_{7/2}\) model space, and solve the quartet BCS variational equations with a charge-independent isovector pairing interaction. The effective pairing strength is constrained from empirical neutron pairing gaps in the Te isotopic chain. We find that the valence quartet number increases as the valence neutron number is enlarged from \(N_{\rm val}=2\) to \(14\). The same increasing behavior is also found for the condensed quartet component. The proton occupation of the \(1g_{7/2}\) orbit is strongly enhanced relative to the conventional like-particle BCS reference and is driven close to the degeneracy-weighted limit. These results suggest that additional valence neutrons enhance the quartet admixture in the correlated quartet BCS state, while redistributing the fixed proton weight from pair-like configurations to quartet configurations.
summary: This theoretical work applies the Quartet BCS framework to model correlations in neutron-rich Tellurium isotopes. It demonstrates that increasing valence neutrons significantly enhances quartet admixtures and alters proton orbital occupation by shifting weight from conventional pair configurations to higher-order quartet terms. This provides a microscopic understanding of enhanced superfluidity in exotic nuclei.
main_problem: The study investigates how quartet correlations develop in neutron-rich Tellurium isotopes, extending beyond standard BCS pairing descriptions.
main_result: Increasing the number of valence neutrons enhances the quartet admixture in the correlated state and causes a redistribution of proton weight from pair-like to quartet configurations.
method: The authors solve variational equations derived from the Quartet Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (qBCS) theory, treating four-body pairing amplitudes explicitly.
model_or_system: The system models valence protons and neutrons in neutron-rich Te isotopes, using a ${}^{100}	ext{Sn}$ core and considering particles in the $2d_{5/2} \oplus 1g_{7/2}$ model space with an isovector pairing interaction.
key_observables: Valence quartet number ($N_Q$), condensed quartet component, proton occupation fraction of the $1g_{7/2}$ orbit ($	ext{P}_{\pi,g}$), and quartet-induced energy gain ($\Delta E_{	ext{Quartet}}$).
important_parameters: The analysis scans the isotopic chain from $^{104}	ext{Te}$ to $^{116}	ext{Te}$, constrained by empirical neutron pairing gaps.
main_assumptions: The theory assumes a charge-independent isovector pairing interaction and neglects isoscalar proton-neutron pairing correlations for simplicity in the initial analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the monotonic increase of $N_Q$ and $\Delta E_{	ext{Quartet}}$ with neutron number, and show how the total proton occupation fraction ($	ext{P}_{\pi,g}$) is composed of pair-like and quartet contributions.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the qBCS framework by solving variational equations for pairing amplitudes. It then calculates key observables like $N_Q$ and $\Delta E_{	ext{Quartet}}$ across an isotopic chain to show increasing correlations, followed by a detailed analysis of proton orbital occupation showing weight redistribution.
why_interesting: The explicit inclusion of four-body (quartet) pairing amplitudes provides a mechanism to enhance correlation effects beyond standard BCS theory, offering insights into exotic nuclear superfluidity analogous to pairing in ultracold Fermi gases.
